test_title: PYST 56: SSC GD Constable - English (Held On - 23 Feb, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: english
question:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.

Wopsle had gone farthest,/ and had better stop in his reckless career/ while there was yet time.

options.text: and had better stop in his reckless career

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the use of the word "**farthest**."
 
• **"Farthest"** typically refers to physical distance. The correct term should be "**furthest**," which can refer to degree or extent in addition to **physical distance.**
 
• The correct phrase should be "**Wopsle had gone furthest**," ensuring grammatical correctness and clarity.
 
• Thus, the error is located in **part 4** of the sentence.

**Correct Sentence:** ***"Wopsle had gone furthest, and had better stop in his reckless career while there was yet time."***

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **1: "while there was yet time."** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **2: "No error"** – This would be the correct option if there were no mistakes in the sentence, but there is an error in part 4.
 
• **3: "and had better stop in his reckless career"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **4: "Wopsle had gone farthest,"** – This part of the sentence contains the error.
